full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J. These two appeals by leave arose out of a common judgment and order dated 26.08.1999 passed in Civil Revision Nos. 761 and 762 of 1989 by the High Court Division making the Rules absolute.

2. The relevant facts are that the plaintiffs filed the suits being Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 for permanent injunction and Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 for declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969, 4th Court of Munsif, Narayangonj, is illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

3. The plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 claimed to have purchased the lands described in the schedule from the admit-ted owners on the basis of a decree passed in Title Suit No. 98 of 1967 by the Court of 2nd Munsif, Narayangonj, followed by execution of the required sale deed as well as delivery of possession through Title Execution Case No. 37 of 1967 and that thereafter one Nur Box sold his share to the plaintiff No. 6 by registered kabala dated 12.01.1970. Thus while the plaintiffs being owners as aforesaid were possessing the suit land detailed in schedule 'A' peacefully, the defendant Nos. 1-7 tried to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land claiming their title thereon on the basis of a decree dated 04.09.1974 passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 and the sale deed obtained through Court on execution; of the said decree vide Execution Case No. 7 of 1975, which fact has been disclosed in the written objection and written statement filed by the defendants in Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and faced with such situation the plaintiffs filed the Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 with prayer for declaring that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 as illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. In the plaint, of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 the plaintiffs included schedules 'A' and 'B', of which schedule 'A' land corresponds to the schedule of P land detailed in the plaint of Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and the lands detailed in schedule-B of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 corresponds to the lands claimed by the defendants, got through execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 vide Title Execution Case No. 7 of 1975. The respondents hereof as defendants contested both the suits by filing written statements. Both the parties adduced witnesses and produced documents, marked exhibits.

4. The contesting defendants of both the suits i.e. Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and Title Suit No. 97 of 1977, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 in the Court of 4th Munsif, Narayangonj, for Specific Performance of Contract, based on a sale-agreement dated 07.12.1963, wherein the plaintiffs of the instant suits were made defendants and they were contesting the suit (Title Suit No. 92 of 1969) and that the said suit was initially dismissed on 21.09.1971 for default. However after liberation of this Country they said suit was restored and ultimately heard and disposed of exparte on 04.09.1974 and the required kabala was obtained through Court by filing Execution Case No. 7 of 1975 covering the lands detailed in the schedule-land of the plaint of Title Suit No.166 of 1976, which is schedule-B land of Title Suit No.97 of 1977.

5. The learned Munsif framed the following issues to arrive at his decision for disposing of both the cases:- (1) Whether the suits as framed and filed are maintainable; (2) Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get decree as prayed for; (3) Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree for permanent injunction as prayed for; and (4) To what other relief(s) the plaintiffs are entitled to.

6. The learned Munsif heard both the cases together and recorded one set of depositions of witnesses for both the cases. On consideration of the materials and evidence available on record and the submissions of the learned Advocates of the respective parties learned Munsif decreed both the suits to the effect that the decree dated 04.09.1974 passed in Title Suit No.92 of 1969 by the 4th Court of made by the learned Advocates of the Munsif, Narayangonj, be declared as illegal, void, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs have acquired right, title and interest in schedule A land and that the defendant Nos.1-6 are permanently restrained, from entering into the schedule-A land.

7. Being aggrieved, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 223 of 1983 against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and Title Appeal No. 224 of 1984 against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 97 of 1977. The appeals were heard one after another and disposed of by a common judgment dated 19.03.1983 dismissing both the appeals holding, amongst others, that the plaintiffs were aware about the Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 and that the plaintiffs were found to be in possession of the suit land.

8. Being aggrieved there against the Civil Revision Cases were filed by the defendants in the High Court Division. The Civil Revision No. 761 of 1989 arose out of the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 224 of 1983 and Civil Revision No. 762 of 1989 arose out of Title Appeal No. 223 of 1983, which were heard one after another and disposed of by the common judgment and order dated 26.08.1999 making both the rules absolute, against which the present appeals were preferred upon obtaining leave.

9. We have perused the impugned judgments passed by the Courts below as well as the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division.

10. We have considered the submissions respective parties. On careful examination of the submissions of the learner Advocates as well as the schedules 'A' 'B', as detailed and or referred to in IV plaints of the Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 and Title Suit No. 92 of 1969, it appeared that out of the plots of land mentioned in the schedule of the plaints, except one plot; other plot are not same. But on the incorrect statement made in the written objection as well as in the written statement filed by the defendants in Title Suit No.166 of 1976 the plaintiffs had to file Title Suit No. 97 1977 for declaring that the judgment as decree dated 04.09.1974 passed in Tit Suit No.92 of 1969 by the Munsif, 4th Court, Narayangonj, as illegal, void fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

11. On consideration of the evidence are materials on record of the cases, appeared that the plaintiffs could not prove their claim that they were not away about the exparte decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 in the year 1974, rather it is found from the copy of the order sheet of Title Suit No. 92 of 1969, annexed to the Additional Paper Boo filed on 12.04.2009 by the Appellants, the after liberation of the Country on restoration of the suit (Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 to its original file and number, since d missed for default earlier, the defender, appeared in the suit on 19.04.1972, 18.07.1972 and 18.12.1973 but did not appear at the hearing and the suit w decreed exparte on 04.09.1974.

12. It appears on comparison of the land described in the schedule of the plaintiff Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 and the lands described in the schedules of plaint of 'We Suit No. 97 and 1977 that the scheduled lands of Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 do of correspond to the lands detailed in Schedule-B of the plaint of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 and those are not same or Common, except one plot being plot N0.158 under Khatian No. 51 measuring 15 decimals as to the lands detailed in Schedule of Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and Schedule-A of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977.

13. The plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 and Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 aimed, to have purchased land measuring 1.58 acres in four plots detailed in schedule-A of the plaint of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 and in the schedule of Title Suit No. 166 of 1976, which are as under:-

15. Thus on comparison of Schedules-A and B detailed above it appears that except the land measuring 0.15 acres in Plot No.168 under Khatian No.51 (underlined), which is a tank, other plots of the schedule 'A' and 'B' are not same.

16. Thus there could not be any cause of action for challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 by the plaintiffs and that the defendants having no claim for any right, title and interest in respect of other three plots of Schedule-A land i.e. plot Nos. 121, 159 and 119 the plaintiffs may get a decree for permanent injunction as prayed for in Title Suit No.166 of 1976 against the defendants in respect of the lands detailed in Schedule-A, except said plot No. 168 under Khatian No. 51 admeasuring 15 decimals, which is described as a pond/ditch, which plot appears to be included in the schedules of both Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 and Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and that the dispute relating to Plot No. 168 under Khatian No. 51 may be resolved separately, if the parties so desire, in a proper forum and in accordance with law.

17. Thus, we are of the view that the plain-tiff-appellants may get a decree for permanent injunction in Title Suit No.166 of 1976 in respect of the Schedule-A lands except said 15 decimals of land being a pond in plot No. 168 under Khatian No. 51 restraining the defendants from interfering illegally or forcibly with the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs thereon. The Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 is liable to be dismissed being barred by limitation, since the record of the Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 shows that the plaintiffs hereof, being defendants in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969, took steps in the suit after its restoration after liberation of the Country in 1972 and thus aware about the decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 in the year 1974 and also for want of cause of action having no proof of any right, title or interest on the lands in reference.

18. Accordingly the Civil Appeal No. 229 of 2002 is dismissed with cost and the Civil Appeal No. 230 of 2002 is allowed in part but without any order as to costs. Thus Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 is dismissed and the Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 is decreed in part. The defendant Nos.1-6 are accordingly restrained permanently from entering into and or interfering with peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in the land detailed in the schedule of the plaint of Title Suit No. 166 of 1976, except Plot No.168 under Khatian No.15 measuring 15 decimals of land. The lands on which injunction in granted, are situated within the District-Dhaka, P.S. Fatullah, Mouja No.152 Pikuni, consisting of 39 decimals (Nal) in Plot No. 121 on the North of which is Audhar Mondal and 56 decimals (Nal) in Plot No. 159 on the North which is Halat and both plots are and Khatian No. 161; and 48 decimals (Nal) Plot No. 119 on the North of which Makhan Mondal under Khatil Nos. 173/189/20 and the total area land which is 1.43 acres.

19. Let the records of the Court below, any received, be sent down immediately.
